primary.derivation: brand-hue = (260 + store logoColor hue) mod 360; set as --store-page-brand-hue on the storefront layout and resolved on .storefront-brand. Ramp shown at the default hue 260.

display.purpose: Hero h1 store name only, sized by name length; the footer full-width name uses the same voice.

headline.purpose: Category titles, Popular, footer Hours & location.

title.purpose: Dish names and prices, modifier group names, totals, brand name, chips (700, 1.125rem).

body.purpose: Descriptions, facts and the hero headline sentence; regular width.

label.purpose: Nav links, metadata, modifier prices, promo banner.

shadows.name: lamp-glow
shadows.purpose: Only on the lit service lamp; it is the open state, not elevation.

motion.name: ease-out
motion.purpose: Press feedback, entrances, ticket drop, plate settle.

motion.name: pass-shutter
motion.value: clip-path inset(0 100% 0 0) to inset(0) 1.1s ease-drawer; child scale 1.12 to 1 over 1.4s ease-out
motion.purpose: Hero plate opens once on load.

motion.name: ticket-drop
motion.purpose: Order ticket contents drop once when the count changes.

motion.name: pass-rise
motion.value: translateY(22px), opacity 0 to 1 on animation-timeline: view(), range entry 5% to 45%
motion.purpose: Section titles and rows rise in; scroll-timeline browsers with no reduced-motion preference only.

motion.name: plate-crossfade
motion.value: opacity and scale 1.03 to 1 over 300ms ease-out
motion.purpose: Sticky menu plate switching to the hovered dish.

tear.purpose: Tooth size of the thermal-ticket mask (conic-gradient, bottom or top edge).

extensions.scope: Guest storefront only. Dashboard and platform pages use a separate shared shell and are not documented.

narrative.overview:
The storefront is the restaurant's pass: the steel shelf under the heat lamps where finished food lands and waits for its ticket. Brushed, cool blue-grey steel is the ground of every food surface. Thermal-ticket paper holds anything a guest reads closely or acts on, set in one near-black ink. The heat lamp's amber appears only as the open-now lamp beside the store name, plus whatever warmth is already in the food photos. The store's own hue fills the one action.

Colour is laid down as flat registered blocks: steel, paper, ink, the store hue, the lamp. No tints, gradients or washes. The photo is one block and the type is the keyblock. Hierarchy comes from scale contrast inside one family. Archivo is condensed and heavy for names, prices and headings, and regular width for everything else. Corners are square, nothing has a shadow at rest, and tickets have a torn edge.

The density is a menu board. Dishes are rows of name and price, and the plate beside the list changes to the dish under the pointer. Facts each get one line in a fixed order (Today, Pickup, Delivery, Address, Rating). The interface speaks only in labels and states.
keyCharacteristics: Steel ground, paper for reading and acting, one ink, the store hue for the one action, amber only for the lamp.
One family (Archivo, variable `wdth`) used two ways: condensed (wdth 68) heavy for names and prices, regular width for text.
Square corners everywhere. Circles appear only for state indicators: the lamp and the radio dot.
No shadows at rest. Depth comes from the paper sitting on the steel.
A torn thermal-ticket edge on the cart button, the hero plate tag, the item panel and the cart sheet.
Tabular figures throughout, so prices line up.

rules.name: The One Hue Rule
rules.body: The store hue fills the one action on a screen (See the menu, Add to order, Checkout) and the focus ring. Nothing else is drawn in it except the single text link on the hero ticket.

rules.name: The Lamp Is State Rule
rules.body: Amber means the kitchen is taking orders. Never use it as an accent, a highlight or a warning colour.

rules.name: The Flat Block Rule
rules.body: Colours are flat blocks. Use no gradients, washes or tinted overlays. The only colour mixes are the action's hover and the lamp's glow.

rules.name: The Two Widths Rule
rules.body: Use the condensed cut for anything that names or prices, and the regular width for anything that explains. Never mix in a second family.

rules.name: The Tabular Price Rule
rules.body: Storefront roots set `font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums`. Prices sit right-aligned on the same baseline as the name.

rules.name: The Paper-on-Steel Rule
rules.body: To lift something, set it on paper over steel. Do not add a shadow.

dos: **Do** set every food surface on steel and every read-or-act surface on paper, with ink text.
**Do** derive the action colour from the store: `oklch(0.47 0.2 var(--store-brand-hue))`. Never hard-code a tenant's hue.
**Do** use the condensed Archivo cut (wdth 68, weight 800 to 900) for names, prices and headings, and the regular width for text.
**Do** keep corners square. The only circles are the lamp and the radio dot.
**Do** give each store fact its own line, in a fixed order, with a fixed label column.
**Do** design for missing data: no photo, no hours, no rating, no delivery, and any name length.
donts: **Don't** use amber for anything except the lit lamp.
**Don't** add shadows, gradients or tinted washes. Lift a surface by setting it on paper over steel.
**Don't** use rounded cards, icon badge rows, or a split hero repeated per category.
**Don't** introduce a second typeface. Don't treat `font-serif` as a serif, because in this storefront it is the condensed Archivo cut.
**Don't** put a second store-hue action on a screen that already has one.
